inputs.text:
Folks, once again we see the left-wing narrative machine twisting things to undermine our sovereignty and national security. We’ve got a case where someone was booked under provisions relating to national security and the Official Secrets Act, allegedly in telephonic contact with a Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri,” and now the progressive establishment is crying foul because the Punjab and Haryana High Court stepped in to grant regular bail. 

The court actually had the audacity to hold that "mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a person in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration." This is the kind of weak-kneed institutional failure that puts our borders and our nation at risk. While the liberal commentariat whines about state paranoia and demands the dismantling of our legal mechanisms in the name of human rights, they completely ignore personal responsibility and the sacred duty of protecting the homeland. When courts start letting people off the hook who are caught communicating across the border under suspicious circumstances, it makes a mockery of national security and the rule of law. We need strong borders, firm authority, and unwavering defense of our country—not coddling suspects who jeopardize our safety.
